utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Registrar, good morning to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, distinguished gentlemen, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You say sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, together with Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, co-counsel, and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink, our case manager. And good morning to the Defence team as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you and thank you. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us today we have our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, as well as our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Vidovic, and good morning to you your team. Before I ask for preliminaries, we promised you yesterday that we would come forward with an oral decision on your oral motion asking for authorisation to reply to the Prosecution response to your motion relating to Rule 68 disclosure and so on. Our decision is in favour of your oral motion, so you can proceed with filing a reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any preliminaries, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any preliminaries on the Defence side? None. Let's bring the witness in, please. Thank you. So how long do you propose to have this witness testify?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I think she'll go for a substantial part of this morning in examination-in-chief. I've got a bit of a video that I want to show to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think you will finish with her this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's certainly my plan, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with regard to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think it will be two hours maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we won't finish with her today. No, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And calm down. You don't need to feel nervous or excited. You are here to give evidence in this case, and I will be explaining to you very soon what the procedure is. In the meantime, as the Presiding Judge it's my duty to inform you that before you proceed with your testimony our rules require that you make a solemn declaration, a declaration equivalent to an oath. A solemn declaration in the sense that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is going to be handed to you now by Madam Usher. Could you kindly please read that solemn declaration aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please sit down. And I take it that you are receiving interpretation in your own language, because obviously I'm speaking in English and most of us will be speaking in English here, and I want to make sure that everything is being translated to you. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. As I tried to explain to you earlier, you're here to give evidence. And the way it works here is very much like it works in your own country and in most other countries. The party that has produced you as a witness will go first, and that will be the Prosecution in this case. Mr. Di Fazio, I take it, will be putting a series of questions to you. And then when he's finished he is going to be asked -- you are going to be asked a number of questions by a member of the Defence team of Mr. Naser Oric, who is the accused in this case. The gentleman you see in the front row here, Mr. Jones, will be the lawyer who will be asking you questions. Your responsibility's a very simple one. You're not here as a witness of the Prosecution; you are a witness of the Tribunal now. So your duty, according to your oath, to your solemn declaration, is to answer all questions truthfully and fully, which I am sure you will do. If you -- at any time you feel tired or if you want a break, just let me know and we'll give you a break. Please try to relax. This is a very simple procedure. You will not have any problems here. Just for your information, my name is Carmel Agius and I come from the island of Malta. To my right is Judge Brydensholt, who comes from Denmark, and to my left is Judge Albin Eser, who comes from Germany. Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Di Fazio will go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just tell me if these personal details that I read out to you are correct. You can just answer with a yes or no. Indeed with all of the questions I put to you this morning, if you can answer with a yes or no, that's fine. If I need more information, I'll ask for it. You were born on the 1st of May, 1968, born in a place called Azlica. You're married to a man named Slavoljub Filipovic. You have a daughter named Olivera who was born in September of 1989 and a son named Nemanja who was born in June 1992. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In December of 1992 you lived in a small village called Bjelovac, reasonably close to Srebrenica, and you lived there in a house with your mother-in-law Dostana Filipovic, your father-in-law Dragoljub Filipovic, and your brother-in-law Dragan Filipovic. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1992, up until about April of 1992, both you and your husband worked in mines in a place called Sase, which is again not too far from Bjelovac and not too far from Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want you to direct your mind now to events that occurred in December of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 14th of December, that's three days prior to the 14th of December, it was a Friday, and the next Monday was the 14th of December. I came to Bjelovac with my children to visit my husband and his parents. I had not been to Bjelovac since April. In the early morning hours on the 14th of December, an attack occurred. There was shooting. I knew instantly that this was an attack. The rest of them --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll get some details that I need. Before we get into the attack itself, I want to ask you something else. Were there any VRS troops stationed in Bjelovac on or about the 14th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just locals, people who lived in the village. I don't know about any soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there a village guard operating in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those people, too, were locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: From time to time when you visited -- came back to your home in Bjelovac throughout 1992, did you see what activities they were up to?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I would only stay briefly whenever I came. I would pick up things for my daughter and for myself. I didn't linger on because there was always at least random shooting going on, therefore I would never stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was your husband, Slavoljub, and your brother-in-law, Dragan, were they members of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they have guns or weapons which they used when carrying out -- which they used when carrying out their job as a village guard?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they take up guarding positions around the village?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They probably did. Those were village guards after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you came back on your visits to Bjelovac, did you see -- would your brother-in-law and your husband leave from time to time to go and carry out guarding duties?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. My husband was at home most of the time and my brother-in-law, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you where your husband and brother-in-law, or indeed any of the other members of the village guard, got their guns from?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think from Bratunac, probably the Territorial Defence. Bratunac probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recall specifically where your husband got his weapon from, or is it just that you think they came from the Bratunac Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He told me on one occasion when I came over that everyone in the village had them from the Territorial Defence in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they have other things such as radios or walkie-talkies?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Uniforms or helmets?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see the village guard training?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want you to turn to the events of the actual attack itself; you started to describe them. It occurred on the 14th of December, 1992. About what time did it start?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it started early in the morning. It was still dark. It could have been any time between 4.30 and 6.00 in the morning. It was still dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who was in your house at the time the attack started? What persons were inside your house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Myself, my children, my husband, my father-in-law, and my mother-in-law. My brother-in-law stood guard that particular night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When the attack started, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I got up. I got the children ready. I woke them up and packed their things up. The next morning I was supposed to go back to Serbia, which is where I lived, near Bovija [phoen], but I could no longer leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did your husband do?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He left the house to see what was going on, but he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he armed when he left the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. He probably took the rifle, but I can't remember. I only looked after the children, but I assume he would have taken the rifle, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And what about the your father-in-law, did he leave the house? And also can you tell us if he was armed or not when he left the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he left the house. He had been in another room, so he left. He was gone after that. Probably he took a rifle with him, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you hear the sounds of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite some.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So upon the attack starting, you and your children and your mother-in-law were the people left inside the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A boy called Brano from the neighbouring house later joined us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'll get to him in just a while. Firstly, from your house -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that. Your house was then constructed with several storeys, several levels?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And from the windows of the house, either on the first or second level, did you have a view of the Drina River and also part of the village of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. We could not see the river Drina from the first floor. There was no view of the Drina River, but there was one from the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So from various points around the house you could actually see out towards the Drina and also into the village itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Only from the upmost floor of the house was there a view of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. During the course of the attack, did you from time to time have occasion to look out the window from any point in the house, looking in any direction, to see what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you see attackers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They wore civilian clothes. Some wore camouflage uniforms. They had ribbons tied around their heads and armbands. When they came into the houses, I saw that some of them had painted faces. Most of them carried weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did that include the men who were dressed as civilians, were they also carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, it was dark when the attack first started. Did -- obviously it eventually became light. Were you still in the house when it was light?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have neighbours with the surname Vucetic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's our next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who's the father of the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Radovan Vucetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And does he have a son called Milenko?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1992, about how old was Milenko?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was about 15 or 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did they also have another son called Brano or Branko?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how old was he?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 7 or 8. I can't be sure, but he was about that age, 7 or 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear about this little boy's name: Was it Brano or Branko or both?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I called him Brano and so did all the other people in the village. Maybe his full official name is Branko. However, I never heard anything but Brano, and I always called him that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, did you during the course of the attack see anything happen to this boy Milenko and his father?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we were still inside the house, the shooting was very intense. We heard people moaning and crying outside in the yard. We knew that somebody was injured. My mother-in-law opened the door and I followed her straight away. This boy Milenko was on his knees on the ground. He said, Don't come out because you'll be killed. He also said his father was injured. My mother-in-law and I went quickly back inside to get some sheets to bandage his wound; however, some of the attackers most have noticed this movement and they started shooting again. My mother-in-law was hurt my shrapnel, I believe, in the leg, and that's when we closed the door and we didn't come out anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the course of the attack, was your house actually shot at with bullets?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the bullets come through windows?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, eventually did the attackers come close to your house or men who were attacking, did they come close to your house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they say anything?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You could hear commotion, racket. You could hear them coming closer and closer. You could hear they were already in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Throughout the -- this -- these events you have been describing so far, was there the sound of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you eventually decide to take refuge upstairs?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was that the whole party in the house, you, your mother-in-law, and the children? Sorry, I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time of this attack on the 14th, were there any weapons inside your house, any type of weapon? I'm not just talking about guns.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There were two hand grenades that I had seen in those two days that I had spent in Bjelovac. And of course the weapons --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just stop there. Sorry -- perhaps I interrupted you prematurely. What other weapons were also in the house, apart from these grenades?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So at the time the attack is actually transpiring, taking place, there are two grenades located in the house. Where are they in the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the room of my father-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that on the ground floor or the upper floor?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just answer my questions now with a yes or no if you can, please. Did you receive any injuries during the course of this attack? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Brano receive any injuries?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did both of you sustain those injuries from a grenade? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have you given statements in the past concerning this attack where you describe the sustaining of these injuries from the grenade? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you provide statements to Serb authorities after you were exchanged -- a statement, I should say, to the Serb authorities shortly after you were exchanged? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I understood you sufficiently well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Just answer yes or no. After you were exchanged in February of 1993, did you provide a statement to the Serb authorities, the Serbian authorities, very shortly after?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, just answer yes or no. Did you provide a statement to a judge in 1994? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in March of the year 2000, did you provide a statement to officers of the Office of the Prosecutor, the ICTY? Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in those statements did you describe the episode of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. injuries sustained by a grenade? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, forgetting about what you might have said in those statements, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber now, as you best recall now, how it was that you sustained those injuries.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When we climbed upstairs, the five of us, we hid in part of the loft that had been built out of wooden panels. However, they already knew that there was somebody inside and they searched the house. When they came in, they saw children's schoolbags. And before they came up, they called out. They said, If there is anyone here, come out and surrender. They searched for a long time without finding us. They warned that they would throw a grenade from a hand-held rocket launcher called Zolja. They warned many times, but we didn't surrender. We didn't come out of the hiding place. Then they left the house and we didn't hear anything else for a while until a very strong explosion from a grenade that fell in to the loft through the roof. Both Brano and I were injured. Brano was sitting behind my back and my mother-in-law was leaning on the wall behind my back. So Brano and I were wounded. I ran into the adjacent room, picked up at random some children's clothing and stuff, rejoined Brano and my mother-in-law. I heard them. They were already in the house by that time. They were furious and they were cursing and swearing. And suddenly one of them said, Oh, that's where they are. He must have noticed the door to the loft. He opened it very slightly and saw us. Then they took us out of the loft and brought us downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to your capture in a moment. You told the Trial Chamber that there were some other grenades that were in the house that I think you said belonged to your husband. Did anything happen in relation to those grenades during the morning of the attack?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When I heard that they were already close, I heard voices in the yard, the first thing that I remembered were those hand grenades. I took them and climbed upstairs and threw them out of the window. One of them hit the floor of the terrace. In any case, I threw them outside. That's how they knew that there was somebody inside and eventually found us. While they were in the yard and while we were still inside, there was a commotion and they must have heard voices.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. So the injuries you sustained were from a grenade that was fired, you presume, by the attackers, not by a grenade that you wielded?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's turn now to your capture. You were, I think, captured upstairs in the loft area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we were wounded, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Because you were taking refuge up there and that's where the bomb exploded. Is that yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of your captors when they first appeared?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The man who detected our hiding place was Mirza Hasanovic. He lived in Sase. I recognised him. I also recognised Sefko Zukanovic. He also lived in Sase and I knew him from school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you know Mirza Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He lived in Sase, and that's only three and a half to four kilometres away from where I lived. We also went to school together in Sase. He is one year younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about the other chap, Zukanovic, how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also from school. He also lived in Sase. His sister went to the same school as I did, so we knew each other well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What ethnicity are those two gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you taken downstairs?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And were you kept there for a while?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a long while.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Were you eventually -- did you eventually leave the house and transfer to another place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Stevo Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Does he live in Bjelovac or did he live in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the day of the attack, did you move from your house to his house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did but later, later that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. That's what I want to know. Now, how long were you kept captive in your house before going to Stevo's house, about how long?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A long time, until 1.00, maybe 1.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It seemed a long time to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Were you guarded during that time that you were in your own house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The house was full. They were coming and going, replacing each other, they were fighting from inside the house from other rooms. There was more than a dozen of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The house was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again tell us, these men, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Some wore civilian clothes, other wore camouflage uniforms, some had paint on their faces, armbands, bandannas, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was Mirza Hasanovic there throughout this period of time that the fighting is going on from inside your house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was, although he came and went occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Did he appear to give orders, commands?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know what weaponry was being used by these men who had come into your house? Was it just firearms or were they using rocket launchers -- grenade launchers, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw rifles which had knives at the end of the barrel, that's the kind of rifle they had. I heard them saying they had weapons called Zoljas, that's a bit longer with a green barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Was -- okay, thank you. During the time that you're in your house, okay, the period of time that you're in your house before you're sent -- you go over to Stevo Filipovic's house, did you hear the sound of airplanes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that you were moved to the house of Stevo Filipovic, and I'll ask you about the movement, the transfer from your house to that house. Firstly, how far away is it from your place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not even 50 metres. It's very close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who transferred from your place to Stevo Filipovic's house, was it all of the soldiers and all of you prisoners or just a portion thereof?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All of us moved to Stevo's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thinking back on all of the events that you saw up until that point, up until the transfer point, so before you went to Filipovic's house, had you seen any houses burning, up until that point?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the occasions when I left my house, I only saw smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So very well then. Let's turn our attention back to the time you transferred from you place to the neighbour's house. When you were making the trip from your house to Stevo Filipovic's house, did you see any houses burning or smoking?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As we were coming out, on the left side I saw a lot of smoke, although it was dark. It was Slavka Matic's house; I think it was her house that was burning. It is right next to my house on the left. I think it was her house that was burning. There was a great deal of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. As you left your house to go to Stevo Filipovic's house, was anything said, said, or done in respect of your house, our own home?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was said or done?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One of the soldiers said, Set the house on fire immediately. We left and I didn't look back because I didn't dare to. But I suppose that's what they did, they set the house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, now -- okay, now you didn't look back. Tell the Trial Chamber why you suppose that. Why do you suppose that? Did you hear anything or see anything that makes you think that or say that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I supposed that because one of the soldiers said to the others, Burn the house immediately. It sounded like an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. So that's one of the soldiers who's been in your house said to another soldier who had been in your house, Burn the house? That's what you heard; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And then you left your house but you didn't actually see it with your eyes burning or being torched?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the trip or the short crossing from your place to the house of Stevo Filipovic, did you see any bodies?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We saw Stevo Filipovic lying near his house, dead. He had an entry and exit wound around his heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you saw him, was he - from what you could see anyway - in uniform, clutching a rifle?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. He was dressing -- he was dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how old was Stevo Filipovic in 1992? You don't have to be precise, but if you can give us an idea if he was a young man or a middle-aged man or an older man.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was in his early 40s.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened to your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was killed. I saw him in the yard of our house as we were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And back in 1992, about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: 50-ish, I think 52 or 53, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was he dressed in uniform or --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Was he carrying or did you see around his body any paraphernalia of war such as a gun, grenades, bullets helmet or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was nothing. He was lying on the ground. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So that's two bodies you've told us that you saw during your transfer from your house to the house of Stevo Filipovic. Did you see any other bodies?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, I did. I saw Slavo Mirdanjanovic [phoen]. I think he was in his early 20s. His year of birth was 1970. He was lying right next to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have the same questions as with the others. Any uniform, any paraphernalia of war, any equipment around him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, the house of Stevo Filipovic, was that intact when you first arrived at it, crossing from your house to it, or was it burning?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Stevo Filipovic's house was already burning, and the upper floor had already burnt down. It was smoldering by the time we came to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you arrived there, were there soldiers inside the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, plenty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again tell us, were they in, as you have described thus far, a combination of men in civilian clothes and camouflage uniforms or were they wearing something else?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well -- okay. Just to be absolutely sure, were they wearing camouflage uniforms and armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there firing of something other than guns, rifles I mean, going on from the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was being fired from the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Later I heard planes flying over. There was a lot of noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We'll get to the planes in just a moment. All I want to know is -- let me ask you directly. Were there any Zoljas being fired from the house, any grenades, rocket-propelled grenades?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were Zoljas around. Later when the planes came, that's when they used Zoljas, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. By the time you got over to the house of Filipovic, Stevo Filipovic, was it daylight?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very much so in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So the scenario at this point is you, your baby, your daughter, and your mother-in-law are in that house surrounded by soldiers apparently fighting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that house for?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Until dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of the time, the period of time that you spent in the house of Stevo Filipovic up until dusk, did you hear the sound of airplanes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At about what time, doing the best you can, did you hear the airplanes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That was later on in the day, quite late in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the soldiers who were -- what you were with show any reaction to the airplanes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had begun to panic and they were frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they say or do anything that indicated to you what -- how they were going to deal with the airplanes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They targeted the airplanes with these Zoljas they had. They positioned themselves at all the windows and they used the windows to fire from, and they were cursing all the time. They were very frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'd like to show the witness an exhibit at this juncture. I'd like to play D11 -- sorry, 111, Defence exhibit. It's a video. Would Your Honours just give me a moment to organise myself, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to show you a video. You've seen parts of it before, I believe. And I don't need sound for this specifically. And I'd like to start at about 5.35. All right. Just go back a bit. Stop it. Now, look at those, what you see now on the screen. Okay. What you can see clearly at least is a row of houses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Di Fazio. We are -- because in the -- previously you said I'd like to start at about 5.35. For the record, we are showing a clip from this video to the witness at 5.44.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if we could go back a little bit to -- my notes are from 12.29 on the -- perhaps at the beginning of 12.29 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- on the video. Just go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is 5.34, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Fine, thanks. We can start here, and I'll ask you to stop in just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, look at that row of houses. Do you recognise any of those places?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, standing in the middle of the frame - that's 12.30 you can see on the time - is a white house, two-storey white house which is not alight and which is seen most clearly. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The person the house belongs to resides in Slovenia. Ever since I came to -- ever since I first came to Bjelovac he was residing in Slovenia throughout. He would only come over once a year for a holiday, but he hails from Bjelovac. He was born there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And next to it is another structure that's plainly aflame. Whose place is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This house belongs to Stevo Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's obviously a mighty powerful flame that you can see there. It's well alight --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we need Mr. Di Fazio's observation. There's smoke. We don't see any flame. Anyway, it's not for him to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps my learned friend is right. I'll retract that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. He's certainly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps I jumped the gun there, if Your Honours please. There's something wrong with the place, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did it look like that when you were being taken over to Stevo Filipovic's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. The upper-most floor had already burned down. There wasn't that much smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we just continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's that in the foreground? Is that the river?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you -- so this particular clip is shot from -- from where, from Serbia or from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours just bear with me. I'd just like to find another portion on the video now; it's at -- should be at about 15.20. All right. We can play.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at this, Witness, and tell us if you can recognise any of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all, that wooded area that you can see, does Bjelovac have a similar wooded area like that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the same wooded area that I can see on the screen right now. That's the wooded area just beyond Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's the little gathering of buildings at the bottom of the screen? What is -- what place is that? Is that Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the houses there?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The one I can see burning in this frame is the house in which I lived. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's your place then?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So again there you can see the house that you've identified as the one as yours. There's another one over on the left on the far edge of the screen. Any idea whose house that is? If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is Stevo Filipovic's house also, the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make this clear: It's not the same house of Stevo Filipovic that we saw burning before, no, it's a different one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Eser would like to ask you a question, Madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us -- could you please tell us in which house did you stay -- in which of Stevo Filipovic's houses? Was it here on the screen? We cannot see it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one that you can see smoke rising from, the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: On the left side there's one, but you told us that this is not the house in which you stayed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's the next one, because Stevo Filipovic owns two houses, and we were in the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And the other one is not on the screen here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We saw it burning before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see smoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it extreme left of the screen, no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: To make it easier, could you just tell us who owns these houses which we see on the screen now? We have one in the middle, in the centre of the picture, and you told us that is your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Then you told us the left there is a house which is -- as I can see is not burning at this moment. Whose house is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Stevo Filipovic's house, one of his houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And the next house at the margin --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is also Stevo Filipovic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And in which of Stevo Filipovic's house did you stay after you have been taken from your own house to Stevo's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one that you are pointing at right now, the other one that you can see smoke rising from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And for the record, the pointer was pointing at what appears to be part of a house in the middle -- extreme left part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think that deals with what --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with D11 -- 111, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Stevo Filipovic's house, could you hear the sound of bombing as opposed to rifle fire or submachine-gun fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did. Those were probably bombs dropped by planes because the explosions were very powerful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. And it's -- it may be difficult -- you may not be able to answer this, but if you can do so. About how far away were the bombs dropping? And if you have any idea where they were dropping, please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not near where we were staying; it was further off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Further off. Can you tell us if further off means further off into the village or further off outside the village or in any particular direction? Again, if you can't answer it -- that, don't; but if you can, tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Further outside the village, that was what I noticed. I saw smoke rising from the wooded area, and that was probably caused by a plane. They did not drop any over the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of that day were you taken outside of the house, Stevo Filipovic's house, at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what was -- what happened when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They had agreed to take me outside and that I should yell for them to stop shooting and that they would in turn allow the Muslim army to retreat into the woods. They brought me out, but my voice was not strong enough to yell. So they took me back to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: While you were inside the house, did the soldiers or your captors describe or speak amongst themselves of their plans, in particular how they intended to get out of the place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were in a panic, they were frightened. They had nowhere left to go. It was an open area and they were only able to stay inside the houses. And so they were very frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they discuss amongst themselves what they planned?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They agreed to stay put, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you've told us already that eventually they left that -- they left that night.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When did -- when was that decision arrived at?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was when they talked, because after all they had nowhere left to go. There was a clearing, an open area, to cross before they reached the woods. So they stayed right there until night fall, hoping that it would be easier for them later on to get across.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How was your baby dressed at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was dressed in bright colours. They ordered me to take these clothes off and discard them so that they wouldn't be noticed in the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you that night eventually leave Bjelovac with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who was -- you've already told us of the people you were with, your mother-in-law and your children. Did they also leave with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And how many soldiers approximately were there with you in the party as you made your way out of Bjelovac at night?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, inside the house there were quite a number. But later we joined up with the rest, the people we caught up with along the way or maybe they caught up with us. At that point in time there were about 20 or 30 of us people who had left their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm about to move on to another topic. Is this an appropriate moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Di Fazio. So, Madam, we are going to have a short break of 25 minutes, during which you can have some coffee and rest a bit. We will resume soon afterwards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's wait for the accused. Yes, let's continue, Mr. Di Fazio. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, before the break we got to the point where you were moving from Stevo Filipovic's house, and you've told us how you left and how you were in a group of soldiers. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We went to the nearby village of Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Approximately how far from Bjelovac is Poloznik?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Six, seven kilometres. I don't know exactly but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the way to Poloznik, did you see any bodies?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Whose bodies did you see?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bodies of Serb civilians from Bjelovac village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of them, who they were?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I could recognise my brother-in-law, Dragan; my neighbour, Milo Sovanovic; my mother-in-law recognised a young girl from the neighbourhood Radenko Jovanovic, nicknamed Duda. She told me that Duda was lying there, but I didn't look because I had seen enough bodies and I was scared. So I didn't really look at the dead body that my mother-in-law pointed out to me; I just passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Of the bodies that you did look at, were any of them in uniform and did they have weapons or bullets or grenades or knives or any sort of soldier's paraphernalia on or around their bodies?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. After all those were civilians from the village dressed in civilian clothes. There were no weapons. I only saw the dead bodies, but I was just passing by and I wasn't looking very closely. I didn't see any weapons in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How old was Dragan, your brother-in-law, in 1992, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was born in 1964, so he was 32 -- sorry. He was born in '62.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. And what about the other gentleman, Milos Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He could have been 60, 61. He was an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you know -- I know that you didn't look at any body you identified as Radenka Jovanovic, but did you know Radenka Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a young girl. I did know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Is Poloznik a small village?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know that village, but there were a couple of houses around where we stayed but I didn't tour the entire village. I don't know how many houses they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Whose house did you go and stay at?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We went to Ramiz's house, Ramiz is a man I knew from before because we worked for the same company in Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know the surname?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I forgot. I used to know it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's okay. That's okay. Anyway, it was a man called Ramiz and you worked with him in Sase. What ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was he there when you arrived in company with the group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I -- you've got to speak up a little bit so that your answer is interpreted. Is that a yes or no? Was Ramiz there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just make sure you speak up so it's -- the interpreters hear it and then it's recorded, okay? Now, you've told us the attack was on the 14th of December, 1992. Can you remember what day of the week that was?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. So, so far the events are these: The attack occurred on the early hours of Monday, the 14th of December; you stayed the day, and you described what happened to you, in Bjelovac; and on the night of the 14th, you made your way to Poloznik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, where were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Ramiz's house all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And on the Friday did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So now I want to take you back to the beginning of your piece -- your period of time in Poloznik at the house of Ramiz on that Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. They are the events I want to ask you about. When you arrived at the house of Ramiz, were there any soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did those soldiers remain in the house of Ramiz throughout the three days that you were there? The three full days that you were there, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you say "soldiers." Tell the Trial Chamber how they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did soldiers -- again, when I say "soldiers," I mean men dressed in camouflage uniforms bearing guns, did they arrive from time to time at the house of Ramiz from the three days that you were there, other soldiers that come into the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any messages being delivered to soldiers in that house by other soldiers who arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you -- were you able to discern or see if any particular soldier in the house was receiving those messages?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For instance, I knew and I heard of a person referred to as Mis, which means mouse. Some messengers came in, handed in some reports. There was also Hazim nicknamed Mrki, who also received very messages from these couriers. And by the way, they spent all their time there in the house, although they occasionally left, but they would always come back in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So the messages seem to be delivered - do I understand you correctly - mainly to Mis and Mrki?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know Mrki's full name?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All I know is that his name was Hazim and that they called him Mrki. Everybody called him Mrki. His home village is Voljavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know any of his family?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there any radio in the house, radio communication, paraphernalia, or equipment?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that operated from time to time?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Throughout --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. How do you know that Mrki was from Voljavica, from the village of Voljavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I later found out that he was originally from Voljavica while I was there in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you find out anything else about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what did you find out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found out that he was very, very close to Naser Oric, that he even acted as his deputy sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know what his normal occupation was in Voljavica before the war? What did he do in Voljavica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about events later in Srebrenica. How long were you actually in Srebrenica for, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In that time did you stay at two houses?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were these -- the owners of the houses that you stayed in, both houses, were they related to Mrki in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the relationship?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were sisters of Hazim, nicknamed Mrki.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in that time, those two months that you were in Srebrenica, did you see Mrki from time to time at the house -- either of -- at the house of either of the two sisters?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll ask you about that in more detail later. There's just one question that His Honour asked you. His Honour asked you: "What did you find out about Mrki?" And you said that: "He was very, very close to Naser Oric. That he even acted as his deputy sometimes." What did you see or hear that makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He spoke of it himself. He said that he was very, very close to Naser Oric and that on many occasions he acted as his deputy. He said that he physically resembled Naser Oric and many people confused them because they were so alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Mrki bearded at the time of your stay in Poloznik?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. A little.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you told us that Mrki spoke about to you -- or spoke about his relationship with Naser Oric on many occasions. Was this later when you were in Srebrenica or did he comment on his relationship during the period of those three days that you were in Poloznik?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Later in Srebrenica, but also in Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. So you arrived during the night, I take it, the night between the Monday and the Tuesday in Poloznik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The next day when daylight came, did you have an opportunity to look around or look outside the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see men in camouflage uniforms who were armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of numbers did you see around the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were coming and going all the time. They were milling around. There were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I'm not asking you to give precise numbers; I know you can't. But can you give us an approximation of the numbers of men that you saw milling around on that Tuesday. Is it a question of 10 or 20 men or 100 men, 5.000 men? Can you just give us an idea.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: More than that, a couple of thousands. They were moving in large groups and large columns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And you were there on the Wednesday and the Thursday as well. Did you see large numbers of soldiers around the house on those days as well or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Later, maybe on Wednesday or Thursday, there were slightly less in number. Smaller groups were left only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one final question. The radio that you said -- that you mentioned, did you see that in use, being used, during the three days, the Tuesday, the Wednesday, the Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, especially by night. They did most of their radio communication by night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Only from secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What secondary school is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I, for instance, went to a vocational secondary school for the catering business, and he went to the butcher's section of the same school. It was the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Is this when you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was metal workers school where Mr. Naser Oric went.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that when you were a teenager?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was in 1983/1984, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And about how long did both of you attend the same institution?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the same school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yeah, I know. But how long were both of you there at the same time? Was it a number of years or weeks or what?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For a year, only a year. I was a younger generation. I just enrolled in that school when he was finishing. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you know any members of his family?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: His younger sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the time that you were at Poloznik, did the name -- was the name Naser Oric mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In what context?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He arrived during the night of the 14th December at the nearby village, Pirici. And he spent the night at his relative's house by the last name of Kurta. I knew these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know any -- the first names of any of the Kurta family?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They are two brothers of Naser Oric, Alija and Izet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Brothers of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Alija and Izet are brothers. Naser spent the night of the 14th of December at the house of the brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How far is Pirici from where you were staying, Poloznik, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe two or three kilometres away, not more than that. Pirici is a place very close to Bjelovac village, the distance is again two or three kilometres. It's closer to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell the Trial Chamber why you say -- why you say this, that Naser Oric spent the night with the Kurta family in Pirici. What's your source of information?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because the soldiers who were staying at Ramiz's house, where I was kept, said, The commander, Oric, arrived last night and spent the night at the house of the Kurta brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about some other people. Do you know a man named Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Speak up, please. What's your answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If you don't speak up loud enough, it's not interpreted. Does he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tursun, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did -- before the war, did you ever see Mr. Tursunovic socially?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I used to see him. He called on sometimes at my father's house; that's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where -- where was your father's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Azlica village, Srebrenica municipality. That's where I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was Mr. Tursunovic's job in those days when he called at your father's house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in our village they were clearing the wood one year. Zulfo Tursunovic worked there with horses that he owned. And they would take timber away from there, clear the timber. Therefore, he would come to my father's house every evening, watch TV, just sit there for a while, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'll turn your mind to Poloznik. On the Tuesday did you see Mr. Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing camouflage uniform and he carried a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he arrive -- I take it he arrived at the house of Razim. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Ramiz. Was he alone or in company with other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was alone when he came to the door, but the soldiers waited for him outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So this is the Tuesday, 15th of December?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did Mr. Tursunovic speak to you or your mother-in-law or your children?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was said?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He yelled from where he was at the door. He said, Where are the prisoners? Let them come out so I can see them. My mother-in-law, the daughter, and myself came out. I brought the small child, too, the baby. He said, Here you are. He asked where we were from, from which family. And they asked if we had any other relatives. My mother-in-law said she had a husband and two sons, and then he asked questions about them. He asked where they are now, and she said they had been killed. He said, Well, that's what they deserved. And then he asked me which family I belonged to, and I said I was her daughter-in-law, that I am Radenko's daughter. And he said he knew my father. And he asked me, Do you remember me? And I said, Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you recall any topics or conversations that were directed to you by Mr. Tursunovic or is that it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He said that we would be transferred at a later stage - he didn't say when exactly - to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right, I see. Was that -- did he say that you would be transferred to Srebrenica towards the end of your encounter with him or the beginning or you can't remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right then, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he say that you would be transferred later to Srebrenica as a result of inquiries about you, from what your fate was to be, or did he just tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he said it himself. I would not have had the courage to ask him myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. How long did your encounter with him last?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a brief one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. During that day were you questioned or spoken to by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you spoken to by a number of soldiers that day? By that I mean men in uniform who were armed.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't spoken to by many soldiers, but quite a number of them kept arriving. And probably the people who spoke to us were people from those units such as Smajo or Mandza. He, for instance, talked to us. On that day, Barak, a man named Barakovic and nicknamed Barak from Jadar was another one. Kemo from Pale - I do remember that - he was another man who spoke to us on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. These are the men I want to ask you about, okay? And doing the best you can, let's go through them in sequence. Is it the case that Zulfo Tursunovic was the first to speak to you or was it one of these other men whose name you have mentioned? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Zulfo Tursunovic was the first, and then others followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They entered the houses later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So of the men whose names you've mentioned, who came after Zulfo Tursunovic as your memory best tells you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who came next, but they followed in a quick succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay then. Well, let me ask you about them individually. You've mentioned one man, Barak. Do you know the actual surname of this man?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Barakovic, and I know that he hailed from Jadar, a village in Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I know because when I returned from captivity in Srebrenica I heard that he was from Jadar. My mother was born in the same village, and I asked whether they had a family of that name over there. And she said that indeed they did, that those were neighbours but they were younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
