utterances.text: But up until that day in Poloznik, that Tuesday the 15th, you had never met this man Barakovic or Barak before?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you recall what he asked you about?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He asked us about our families and which members of our families were still in Bjelovac at the time, whether there were any soldiers and whether they were armed. That sort of question, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned another name, Kemo. Firstly, do you know -- I take it that Kemo is a nickname. Do you know this guy's -- this gentleman's full name?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had you heard about him prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What had you heard about him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard when I was younger - I was still going to school - that he caused a lot of trouble, incidents. And I also heard that he had once killed a man in a bar. He was a man prone to such outbursts of rage and punch-ups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had you actually seen him or laid eyes on him prior to this day in Poloznik? Had you physically seen him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't know that man, not personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, at the time that you were being questioned by Kemo, did you know that he was the same Kemo whom you had heard about in your younger days?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So he was just a face to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And when did you find out that in fact this person who spoke to you in Poloznik was in fact Kemo and how did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I found out later when I was in Srebrenica or at Solocusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who told you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hazim, also known as Mrki, was the one who told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what precisely did he tell you? What did he say to you or what happened that made you put two and two together, that made you conclude, Okay, the man that I used to know about, that I'd heard about as a younger girl was in fact the same guy who interviewed me on Tuesday, the 15th, in Poloznik, that it was in fact Kemo. How did you make the connection?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hazim once said when he came to visit us that in Potocari there was some prisoners - and he was talking about Kemo - and that there was some young girls among those prisoners over there. They had to lock them up to save them from Kemo who apparently wanted to kill them. This apparently was the reason why they had to lock them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, that might explain that you heard more bad things about Kemo, but it doesn't explain to the Trial Chamber how it is that you know that one of the guards -- one of the men who came and spoke to you on that Tuesday was Kemo. You knew Zulfo because you'd seen him before at your father's house. How did you know that the man that came and spoke to you was Kemo?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hazim, called Mrki, told me. I described his physical appearance, and he confirmed that this was indeed the same person. I told him that he was a horrifying man, or rather very serious at first glance. I explained what his physical appearance was like, and Hazim confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did the man you believe is Kemo, what did he ask you about?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the usual sort of thing, like everyone else, who was in Bjelovac, what sort of weapons did they have, what really happened over there, more or less the same questions as everyone else. How many soldiers were around, if any, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you were being asked questions by the man you believe is Kemo, was he holding anything?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A large knife, and he also carried another weapon, a rifle, but he certainly did have a very long knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he do anything with it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He fiddled with it from one hand to the other. He kept fidgeting with that knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's enough about Kemo. You mentioned another man who -- I believe, who spoke to you was a gentleman named Smajo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Smajo Madzic also known as Madza; that's what everyone called him. Smajo Mandzic nicknamed Mandza [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did I hear you correctly, was it Smajo Madzic or Smajo Mandzic, M-a-n?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, prior to this encounter, had you ever met him or seen him before?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How do you know his name was Smajo Mandzic and that he was known as Mandza?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He introduced himself. I heard other people referring to him as Mandza, so then he introduced himself. He had a brother named Kiram, at least I think his name was Kiram but I may be wrong about this. He worked at the Sase mine. And when he heard I worked at the mine, too, he asked me if I knew his brother and I said I did. And then he explained that this was indeed his brother. But the point is he introduced himself, that's how I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Again, can you tell us what he asked you about.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The same questions. All of those questions were the same for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned the name Mrki. Was he there on this Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you questioned by him at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So far you've told us of these encounters between you and these men who you've told us about. Was your mother-in-law also questioned or was it just you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Both. Both separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've told us about the information that you heard about Mr. Oric regarding where he had stayed overnight. Other than that occasion, did you hear Mr. Oric being discussed by the soldiers in any context whatsoever during the three days that you were in Poloznik?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: These men that interrogated you, did you see them from time to time over the next three days?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not all of them, but I did see Mrki, Mis, and Mandza again from time to time over the following days. Mis and Mrki were there the whole time. Sometimes every now and then they would leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You saw -- you described earlier in your evidence messengers arriving. Did messengers continue to arrive, come and go, from the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Usually at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And apart from the encounter with Kemo and when he was -- with the knife, were you mistreated or any -- or your mother-in-law or your children in those three days that you were there in the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want you to turn your attention now to the Friday. You've already told us that that's the day that you went to Srebrenica. So it's --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's the 18th; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you get from your location in Poloznik to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in a yellow car, a Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all, did -- did you travel in the yellow Mercedes from Poloznik all the way to Srebrenica, or did you pick up the car at some later point?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The whole time, from my house to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mean from the house of -- in Poloznik to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who was driving the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were any other of those men you've described in the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mrki sat on the passenger's seat, and the five of us were seated at the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I realise I've omitted to explain one important matter. You mentioned earlier in your evidence -- you mentioned earlier in your evidence there was a little boy who was injured about the same time you were in your house, and his name was Brano. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Brano with you from the time that you were taken from your house to the house of Stevo Filipovic, and from Stevo Filipovic's house to the house in Poloznik and then --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So I've only been referring to your mother-in-law and your children so far, but in fact the group of captives wasn't just that, it was you, your mother-in-law, your little boy Nemanja, your daughter Olivera, and this little boy Brano?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And that's the group that was in the back seat of the yellow Mercedes?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the drive take you through Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you see out of the window of the car?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber what you could see of the houses, what sort of condition they were in as you drove through Bjelovac on your way to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the houses had been burnt. Those that had not been burned had no windows. We met a lot of passers-by on the way, women walking along the road, soldiers, too. Women were carrying bags. Probably they were in the process of looting. Soldiers were carrying things, too, sacks and bags. As for the houses, most of the houses had been burnt. There was smoke smoldering from some, but not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about your house? Did you see your house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the house I really wanted to see, so I paid close attention. The second floor had burned down and all the woodwork had burned down, too. So, yes, I did see the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Now, I just want a bit more detail about what you saw. Is it your position that most of the houses in the village had some fire damage from what you could see? Is that how I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do I also understand you correctly that they appeared to be damaged but were not smoldering, apart from a small number of houses that were still smoldering?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You said you saw civilians. Did that include men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they have bags?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Quite many.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians inside houses or apparently going into a house or looting a house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see these civilians carrying bags whilst the car's actually travelling through the village of Bjelovac? Did you see these civilians carrying bags in the village of the Bjelovac, not on the road to Bjelovac or on the road from Bjelovac, but inside the village of Bjelovac, did you see civilians carrying bags?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: At the same time, and again I stress inside the village of Bjelovac, at the same time that you saw these civilians carrying bags did you see soldiers in camouflage uniforms bearing arms?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I take it that you continued through the town and continued on the road to Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the road to Srebrenica as you're travelling along in the yellow Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mercedes, did you civilians carrying bags?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. We mostly came across small groups of soldiers, not large groups, small groups heading for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were these men dressed in camouflage uniforms and armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There were men in camouflage uniforms and some were wearing civilian clothes, but all were bearing arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were any of them carrying bags?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps rucksacks, but -- yes, rucksacks and backpacks slung over their shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And were these small groups of men from time to time -- that you would see from time to time along the road as you approached Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Small groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About what time of the day did you arrive in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime, not too early and not too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, before you move to the next set of questions, Judge Eser would like to ask a couple of questions in relation to the location of the various places on the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to have a question with regard to the tour which you took from Poloznik to Srebrenica. And it would be helpful to have Exhibit P45, P405. Could perhaps give the map to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours mind if I just had a brief look at it before it's handed to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You can also give it to the Defence before ... It's only just to make clear where we are, where they were are moving around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You had -- Mr. Di Fazio, you had indicated that you would be making use of a map --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we have no indication of which map -- I think you had better show it first to Mr. Di Fazio because it has got markings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think I'm okay. I've got a copy. It can be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The markings are not important for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. But they may have objections, either the Defence or the Prosecution. So we show them first to the parties. Do you have any objection of making use of that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Absolutely none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Since it has got markings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: None at all. In fact, I think it would be a fairly useful exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. But, of course, I need the go-ahead. So, usher, you can show that map to the witness. Maybe we can put it on the ELMO and then we can zoom in the area or the part of the map that we will be dealing with. I think I can direct straight away the technicians to move a little bit the map -- yes, exactly. Centre the marked part and when we tell you to zoom in -- yes, that's perfect. You could leave it at that for the time being. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Stojanovic, could you perhaps locate the place Poloznik? You are very close to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Could you now locate Srebrenica. It's not on the map now. The map should be moved further up -- yes, here. And now you told us that you drove from Poloznik to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And now my first question is: It looks a little bit strange that you went this long way from Poloznik to Bjelovac and then to Srebrenica, although it would be -- it looks much closer from Poloznik to Srebrenica if you would go directly. So you took a long detour via Bjelovac. Did you find Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: If you go one to the north.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be right here, but I can't see any writing. Here it is, Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, if you look here, it is a little bit strange, at least you may wonder why you did not take a direct route from Poloznik to Srebrenica because it's west of Srebrenica, is west of Poloznik. And instead you went from Poloznik to Bjelovac. Is that because there's no direct road between Poloznik and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, but I can point out for you all the places that we drove through if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the places along the road, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And when you spoke of houses burning, could you identify the villages where you saw houses burned down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bjelovac, Bjelovac. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Biljaca. Here we can see Sase where it says "lead and zinc," and then Gradina, Azlica, Zalazje, and finally Srebrenica. So these are the villages we drove through en route. And these are villages that I am indeed very familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: In which villages did you see either houses burning or that people would take away or were carrying certain things, in which of these villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bjelovac, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Only in Bjelovac or also in other villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Only that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But, there's one point that I didn't understand, Madam. Under normal circumstances someone who wanted to go from Poloznik to Srebrenica with his own car, would he have gone the same route, the same way you went to Srebrenica on that day; or is there a more direct approach that he could take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what you mean now. The road that we took to Srebrenica is passable asphalt road; whereas, the road from Poloznik to Bjelovac is a track, a macadam road, through the woods. And it's probably the same kind of road directly from Poloznik to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that area that well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. But had you been to Srebrenica before in your life, before that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until what day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until you were taken to Srebrenica from Poloznik. Had you been to Srebrenica before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's where I went to secondary school. I lived close to Srebrenica, only eight kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You had never travelled by car from Poloznik to Srebrenica direct, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I never went up there. That was the first time that I was in Poloznik. I had never been there before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think we can move to where we interrupted you, Mr. Di Fazio. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, actually. In fact, if I might ask one question just while you've got the map there P45 -- oh, sorry, P450.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay. P450.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier another village that was apparently quite close to Poloznik called Pirici. Can you see that on the map? Or Pirici?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you show the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have to find it. Yes, this is the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Usher, I've finished with the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. So now I want to take you to your arrival in Srebrenica. Where in Srebrenica were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We were taken into a building that is right next to the town hall, the municipality building, where we were interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A man I knew from before, Hamed Hasanovic. I knew him from school, and we also worked in the same company in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were taken in the car, the yellow Mercedes, with two men you've described as soldiers, Mis and Mrki. Did Mis and Mrki deliver your party, the group of captives, to Mr. Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So it was them that took you to this interpretation, not only transporting you to Srebrenica - I know that you've said that - but once you got to Srebrenica it was them, Mis and Mrki, who handed you over to the interrogator. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did Hasanovic interrogate you for a while?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Questioned you. And what about your mother-in-law, Dostana Filipovic, was she also questioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of topics were covered during the questioning?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He asked us where we were coming from, what were the members of our family, if there was any army in Bjelovac, in Bratunac, how well they were armed. He asked about many missing Muslims, mentioning them by name. But we were not able to answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. What about the personal details from yourself and your children. Did you -- were you asked about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He also asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And Brano was there as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long were you questioned for?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not a very long time because we couldn't answer most of the questions. We didn't know anything, so it didn't take long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the questioning, were the two men, Mis and Mrki, present?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were. They came and went, but they were around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to where you, I mean -- by that I mean the party of captives, Brano and your mother-in-law and so on, would stay? Where you would be kept?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they talked among themselves. They discussed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you say that, they talked amongst themselves, did Mis and Mrki, the army -- the soldiers participate in those discussions concerning where you were going to be kept?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They talked about that and they were trying to decide where they were going to keep us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And was a decision finally reached?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please repeat his question. The interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sure. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where were you finally taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They took us to Solocusa, to the house of Hazim's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Her husband's name was Mujo; I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is Hazim Mrki?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is. And Mis, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Hang on. Isn't -- there was only one Mis, that's the soldier who was in Poloznik, and drove you in the yellow Mercedes to Srebrenica. One person called Mis. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's the man who took us to Solocusa, Mis, with the same car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. And Solocusa, is that just on the outskirts of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's perhaps two kilometres before Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you remember who -- of the party who went to this house? Was it you, your children, Brano, and your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this area Solocusa, was that the area, apart from switching from one house to the other, that you basically stayed in for the next two months?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And the two houses in Solocusa that you stayed at in the next two months were both owned by the two sisters of Mrki. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did they have their own families living there, husband and children?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. The next day after you'd been -- the next day you were in Srebrenica, were you taken back for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who came and collected you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The same men, Hazim and Mis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They took us again to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And where in Srebrenica were you taken?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For repeated interrogation in the SUP building. They questioned us there again and took us again to Hamed's, where we had been the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did your mother-in-law come back with you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. On that day she stayed back in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because they separated us then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you see her again until your exchange?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw her in the building of the SUP. I gave her some pills that she needed and that had stayed on me. I was about two or three days late.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at this photo from Exhibit P419, in particular photo 03617712 which is on the screen -- should be on the screen shortly. Do you recognise any of the locations that you can see in that photo?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the right-hand side is the town hall of Srebrenica, the municipality building, and on the left-hand side is the building where we were interrogated, however the entrance was further up. So it's the building on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know where your mother-in-law was kept during her time in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: She was kept in prison, together with all the other captives.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I don't know where the other captives were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And looking down the end of the little laneway that separates the two buildings you've talked about beyond the white car is another building that appears to have a pink addition on top. Do you recognise that -- part -- that part of that building?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's probably a house. I don't know. I know it from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've finished with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You were telling us about an occasion when you took pills to your mother-in-law. How did you accomplish that? How did you get the pills and how did you get from Solocusa to wherever your mother-in-law was being kept? How did you manage that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We walked there from Solocusa to Srebrenica. Hazim, nicknamed Mrki, came and said that she was ill and that she asked me to send back the pills. And I asked him for permission to go and see her. I went there, I gave her the pills, and from that day until the exchange, we didn't meet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you accompanied when you went to speak to her? Were you accompanied when you took the pills to her or were you allowed to go by yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hazim, also known as Mrki, accompanied me, both there and back. And he was present during our encounter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I know it's a little early, but I'm about to move on to some topics that involve documents, and I'd prefer to be able to march through my thoughts about that. I'm happy to say that it's going as planned and I expect to be finished today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And more or less you still are where you thought earlier on this morning? Two hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It might be slightly more, perhaps two and a half hours, but we have plenty of time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will be able to finish tomorrow, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's for sure. If Mr. Di Fazio finishes today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, obviously, obviously. Okay. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry about the delay, but I got held up on something urgent. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've just been looking at my notes and what I've got left. I think that I'll be lucky to finish today. If I go over, though, I'd just like to allay your fears that if that happens it's not going to take me very long to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you're going to finish today, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at a document that I produced to you. It bears 02075680 as ERN number. Copies should be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to say, Your Honour, that our objections to documents from the Sokolac collection are on the record and will emerge also in the course of cross-examination, but just so that is noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And apparently this document can also be viewed on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you have the document in front of you. Have you -- prior to coming here to The Hague, had you ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It apparently says on the face of it that it's dealing with certain persons. I want to run the names by you. Do you know a person named Stana Mitrovic, father Slavko. Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about the next name down the document, Mara Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What about the third name - I think you know her name - Dostana Filipovic, that's your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In that paragraph there's some information there concerning your family and your family life. In the second sentence it says that your mother-in-law Dostana took care of the children in the apartment in Bjelovac when you weren't there. Did that ever happen? Did she baby-sit for you from time to time? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the question. Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Read the second -- the last paragraph. You see there it's talking about Dostana Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. She -- it says that she is the mother-in-law of a person called Mira Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Mira Filipovic, not Mira Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Exactly. I was going to ask you about. Is Radovic your maiden name or is it any name you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go straight to the document, Mr. Di Fazio. Look at the second sentence in that paragraph, please, which starts [B/C/S spoken]. Do you agree with what is written there? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why isn't it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I don't understand when my mother-in-law looked after my children. While I was at work, she did look after my daughter, but that was while I was still employed and working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, she is back to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender the document, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This has not been marked or pre-marked. Not yet. So this will be P?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be P468.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I move on to the next document while that's being dealt with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like to produce another document to you. And for the purposes of the record that bears ERN 02075738. Now, look at that document, please. That is in fact almost identical to the document I showed you before, but it also bears some handwriting. And it's the handwriting that I'm interested in. And you see that underneath the paragraph dealing with Stana Mitrovic, Mara Obradovic, and Dostana Filipovic, someone had written in handwriting: Exchanged on 7th of March, 1993, at Vitez. Do you see that handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I haven't yet got to your exchange, but I will shortly. But were you -- think carefully about this question. Can you tell the Judges, yes, I was exchanged on the 7th of March; or is it the case that you don't know when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when I was exchanged, but it was certainly in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I was exchanged together with my mother-in-law and with the children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you are probably looking at the English translation of the original. But in the original, while the first one, Stana Mitrovic, is shown to be exchanged on the 7th of March, the other two, the date is 7th of February and not the 7th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. I'm sorry. I was misled by the English. I'm grateful, Your Honour, for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I think I might have misled you, too, Witness. In fact, if you look at the entries that come under the name of Obradovic and Filipovic, the date says there -- there's a reference to an exchange at Vitez on the 7th of February, 1993. Now, could that be the date on which you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. The month was February, and the year is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know this place, Vitez? Do you know of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not really. I thought, for instance, that I was exchanged at Jezero because I knew that place and I thought it was Jezero. I didn't know Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where's -- and what is Jezero? Is that a village, an area, a lake, a mountain? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I certainly seek to, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be marked as P469. Just for the record, it's being pointed out that while the previous document was dated 9th February, this one is dated 3rd February and it refers to exchanges that took place allegedly on the 7th of February and in the first part, 7th of March of 1993. Yes, go ahead, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Before we leave this document, there's something else a little bit strange. If you go to the Serbian version, the Serbian -- the date is 3rd of February, 1993, and if you come down under Mitrovic who was exchanged, it reads like 6th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, that is so. That is so, if Your Honours please. I don't think that I can elicit any explanation from this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly not. Just point it out for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Can we move on now and the witness be shown P157. Could Your Honours just bear with me briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this particular document contains some details about your life in Srebrenica in those two months, and that's what I want to ask you about. Firstly, your father's name -- is your father's name Radojko?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And your mother-in-law, what was her maiden name?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Go to paragraph 2 of this document, and it says that you and your children and Brano are going to be accommodated with someone called Hamiz Omerovic from Voljavica? Who's that? Who's Hamiz Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Hazim, it's probably the person known as Mrki. I didn't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And is he -- did you say earlier that he's from Voljavica? Is that what you understood?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know the full name of Mis?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. Can the witness be shown document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is -- has this been tendered or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's in evidence. It's P157.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now can I produce to you document bearing ERN number 02075729. Now, again there are details that touch upon your personal circumstances. Olivera's father, what's her -- what's the name of the father of Nemanja and Olivera?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Slavoljub. Radojko is the name of my father, so there's an error here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Radojko is your father's name. Thank you. Now, was Olivera born in 1970?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, in 1989. This is again a mistake. The date given for Nemanja is correct, although the father's name is Slavoljub, not Radojko. Vucetic, Brano, son of Radovan, that's correct. But I don't know in which year he was born. It says 1983 here, it may be correct. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And what about the last entry, do you know Branimir Mitrovic, father Svetozar. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, that one wasn't with us. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And go to the bottom of the document. Again, there's a handwritten note says: "Exchanged at Jezero (Toplica) on 7th February 1993." Have you ever heard of Toplica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that close to Jezero?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where it is, but I heard about a place called Toplica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And could you just briefly look at this map that I want to produce to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. It should be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be 470.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And incidentally, if -- there's an obvious indication that the date of the four individuals mentioned in this document is wrong, because if the Olivera Filipovic was indeed born in 1970, she wouldn't be underage in February of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: She just touched upon that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: She said that was wrong and the child was born in 1989. Thank you. Could you put this map that I now produce on to you on the ELMO. And for the assistance of Ms. Usher, the area that I want is the bottom part of this map in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you indicate, looking at that map, if you know where Jezero is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I might ask the usher to take this marker pen and give it to the witness. And if the witness can indicate where Jezero is, to circle it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see Toplica anywhere nearby? Good. Circle that, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Circle Toplica.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could -- between Toplica and Jezero, could you put your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you do as His Honour asked you to, put your initials in between the two markings, Toplica and Jezero.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. I'll -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I seek to tender that map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be P471.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll return to your exchange very briefly in a short while. I just want to ask you about one or two matters concerning your time in Srebrenica. Do you know a man named Enes Karic?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During your time in captivity -- sorry, your time in Srebrenica, did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We knew each other as work colleagues. He used to work in Sase, too. While we were in Srebrenica, he came to see us once.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. And was that a social call?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He himself said that he was working on the police force. He was wearing a police uniform, and he must have come to see how we were doing and if anybody was treating us badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he tell you of the circumstances under which he came to be visiting you, how it was that he got to the house to visit you in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything about that. But he said that he was working on the police force in Srebrenica, and you could tell by his uniform that he was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he mention anything else to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did he visit?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was it easy for him to visit you as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I want to take you now to the exchange that we've just been speaking about. Who informed you that you were to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Smajo Mandzic, nicknamed Mandza. He came that morning, not very early in the morning. He said, You have two minutes to get ready. You are going to be exchanged. I picked up my children. We left the house, and we drove in his van to Srebrenica where we stopped outside the building of the municipal government. There were a lot of people, and the likelihood was high that all of them were prisoners. They had a paper in their hands from which they read names, and out of that large group of people, people came out one by one and got into the van. Around 20 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fine. Just hold it there. I want to get a few more details. Who held the list and read out the names; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there men in uniform who were also armed in and around this group?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the man who was reading from the list in camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was your name on the list?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe. But I didn't hear it because I was sitting in the van all the time. I never got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was Brano with you and your children?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you see your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: She also got into the van eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What condition was she in when you saw her?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: She had changed a lot. Her face seemed to have grown darker. It's like she had aged in a short time and lost a lot of weight. She looked awful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you taken in the van to the point of exchange?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who drove the van?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember whether it was Mandza or somebody else took over, but he was also with us in the van.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mandza was also with you in the van?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was with us in the van. And I think he was the one responsible for the exchange because he was the one who handed us over to Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there any other men in camouflage uniform who were also armed accompanying the group?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There were a few, not too many, though. A few, three or four, they were armed and in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Inside the van?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Inside the van, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did -- was the exchange relatively uneventful? You were handed over and other people came walking in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In addition, was there a corpse to be exchanged with your group?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The 20 of us were exchanged plus a dead body. And on the other side there were dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Following the exchange, were you taken to a hospital and medically examined?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And did you discover that you had pieces of shrapnel in your body?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where? Where in your body?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The left side of my body, a centimetre from my heart and lungs, my head, and one of my arms and one of my legs, all on the left side of my body.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you still carry pieces of that shrapnel in your body?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: After the exchange did you see the boy Brano again?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not right after, but I do see him now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've just got a few more questions to put to you, if you don't mind, and then perhaps we'll finish for the day at that point if it's suitable. Thank you. Did you ever receive any compensation for the damage that was caused to your house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Compensation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, compensation. Any sort of compensation.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Construction material was donated, so we built a new house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you have any idea, any good idea, who it was who donated that material?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am not entirely sure. Some organisation or other. I can't be more specific. I think the name was Mercy Corps or something like that. It was a donation of construction material for the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And have you since then been able to reconstruct a house and a home for yourself back in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can stop here. There's no point in starting now, also because the witness, I notice, is -- needs a rest. So we are still where we are. Tomorrow you think you can finish in about two hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. So, Madam, we are finished for today. Now you will be escorted back to your hotel and you will return tomorrow morning. We will certainly finish with your testimony tomorrow morning, and you will be then able to return back home. Take a good rest, and tomorrow we should be in the courtroom for less time that you were today. I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's it. We continue tomorrow morning. We adjourn until tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of January, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.35 p.m.,
